question:
What is the standard Japanese pitch accent pattern of 「弟」?

Answer Choices:
A. Heiban
B. Atamadaka
C. Nakadaka
D. Odaka
E. Heiban or Nakadaka

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The word 「弟」 (otōto) consists of four morae (お・と・う・と). In standard Tokyo Japanese, it follows either the heiban pattern (LHHH, no pitch fall within the word) or the nakadaka pattern (LHLL, fall after the second mora). Both realizations are widely attested and accepted as standard, so the correct choice is E. 

(The other patterns can be ruled out immediately: it does not begin with a high pitch (eliminating atamadaka), the fall is never after the final mora (eliminating odaka), and it is not uniformly heiban with no variation.)

2.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Nakadaka. 「弟」 is pronounced with four moras (o-to-u-to), and the standard pattern places the pitch peak on the second mora before dropping, which aligns with Nakadaka rather than a post-final drop. This is consistent with similar kinship terms like 「姉」 that also follow Nakadaka when unaccented particles follow.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Heiban

「弟」 (otōto) consists of four moras (お・と・う・と). In standard Tokyo Japanese it follows the heiban (平板) pattern: the pitch is low on the first mora and rises on the second, remaining high through the end of the word (L H H H). When a particle is added the pitch stays high, confirming there is no accent kernel. This matches the type-0 entry found in standard accent dictionaries (NHK, Shin Meikai, etc.). The other patterns (atamadaka, nakadaka, odaka) produce audible drops that do not occur in the canonical pronunciation.

Final answer: A
